title: Driver Cab Layout and Control Groups
summary: Identify the driving desk, traction/braking controller, door controls, display panel and safety indications.
objectives: Explain how controls differ from feedback instruments
Recognize the purpose of a safety-critical switch

sections.heading: Driving desk and working zones
sections.body: The driving desk groups frequently used controls near the operator and places information where it can be read promptly. A typical arrangement includes a master controller, train speed indication, door controls, brake indications and warning lamps.
points: Movement controls request traction, neutral and braking.
Instruments provide speed and system indications.
Safety controls are designed for abnormal conditions.

sections.heading: Master controller area
sections.body: The combined master controller has thirteen detents: P1–P4 for power, N for neutral, B1–B7 for service braking, and EB for emergency braking.

sections.heading: Door and safety controls
sections.body: A door bank must be enabled before OPEN can be requested at standstill; CLOSE secures it again. The master handle EB position or Security Brake button applies emergency braking. After a stop and N selection, a separate release control permits the three-second emergency-brake release. The All Doors Closed indicator reports that both door banks are secured.

sections.heading: Reading the front panel
sections.body: Speed, braking indications, master-controller status and warning messages support the driving task. Display designs differ between vehicles; always interpret a reading according to its label, units and the particular train system.

reviewQuestions.question: Which item requests movement or braking?
reviewQuestions.explanation: The handle is an operating control; the other items are indications.

reviewQuestions.question: Where would a driver verify a completed passenger-door closure?
reviewQuestions.explanation: Door-closed feedback is a status indication, distinct from the Close request.
